Independent bounded reproduction: compute digit sums by repeated quotient/remainder for n=0,…,1500 for all reduced 1≤a<b≤17; accumulate successive unequal bits and verify the all-prefix identity or all-odd alternation. 142595 checks over 95 radices, no mismatch.
correctness.rationale: The Euclidean digit recursion gives the last-digit parity plus the bit at q(n)=floor(an/b). As n runs from 0 to M−1, q(n) stays still or rises by one, with its rising edges covering exactly the q(M) input edges. The last-digit difference is a−b[q(n+1)−q(n)]. For even a, a stationary edge contributes zero and a rising edge contributes the complement of its input change. For even b, a stationary edge contributes one and a rising edge contributes the complement. This directly proves C(M)+C(q(M))=q(M) for even a, or =M for even b, a check also valid off the block grid and at M=0. At M=bN this gives the claimed identity. With β=t/(a+b), the all-prefix relation gives E(M)=−E(q(M))+O(1), and q contracts geometrically to zero, yielding the claimed logarithmic discrepancy. The difference between counts of 01 and 10 telescopes to the endpoint bit difference. For odd a,b, induction through the same recursion proves x(n)=n mod 2. No separate mixed-parity equal-pair frequencies follow from this argument.
residual_risks: Finite checks do not establish the infinite-family result. The error is an upper bound for each fixed radix, not asserted sharp nor uniform in a,b.

value.rationale: Exact transition statistics are natural in rational-base parity words, for which full pattern-frequency questions are nontrivial. The identity determines every radix's leading transition frequency with an effective sublinear error without relying on separate single-bit or equal-pair frequencies, and classifies the radically different both-odd case. The useful new benchmark is universal, not its already implied isolated 3/2 value.
residual_risks: Does not address separate 00 and 11 frequencies or general pattern frequencies; the reported discrepancy order is not a sharpness claim.
